fed_news.headline: Treasury selloff signals need to bolster Fed's inflation credibility, Musalem tells Reuters
fed_news.summary: St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the Treasury selloff underscored the need to reinforce the Fed's inflation credibility. Reuters reported that CME FedWatch implied a 67% chance of a 25bp hike at the September meeting.

fed_news.headline: Fed dissenters sketch the case for a rate hike
fed_news.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she dissented in favor of a 25bp hike because inflation remained too high and was unlikely to return to target without tighter policy. She was one of three officials who dissented at the July meeting.

fed_news.headline: J.P.Morgan brings forward Fed rate hike call to December after July hold
fed_news.summary: J.P. Morgan now expects a quarter-point hike in December 2026 rather than in the second half of 2027, while flagging September hike risk remains live if inflation continues to run hot. Markets priced a 65.2% chance of a September hike, down from 81% before the July statement.

fed_news.headline: Dollar recovers as Fed holds rates, US strikes Iran
fed_news.summary: The dollar steadied after the Fed's hold decision and a US strike on Iran-linked targets added to geopolitical risk premium in markets. Fed funds futures imply a 42.6% probability of a hold at the September meeting, compared with 24% before the July decision.

fed_news.headline: The most hawkish split in a decade: the Fed holds steady with three dissents
fed_news.summary: The FOMC held the target range at 3.50%-3.75% on a 9-3 vote, the most divided vote in over a decade, with three regional presidents dissenting in favor of an immediate 25bp hike. Odds of a September hike stood near 70% pre-decision on CME FedWatch.

fed_news.headline: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady at July FOMC meeting
fed_news.summary: The Fed held its target range at 3.50%-3.75% for a fifth consecutive meeting, in a 9-3 vote with three dissents favoring a hike. Chair Kevin Warsh held a press conference at 2:30pm ET. No meeting is scheduled in August; the next meeting is September 15-16, 2026.

fed_news.headline: What a divided Fed means for investors
fed_news.summary: Following the hawkish hold, Fed funds futures suggested a more than 57% likelihood of a quarter-point hike at the September meeting, per CME's FedWatch tool. About 53% of Kalshi traders predicted a hike versus 43% for another hold.

fed_news.headline: Fed's hawkish hold and global market reactions
fed_news.summary: Treasury yields jumped after the decision, with the 30-year approaching its highest level since 2007 near 5.10%, and futures pricing roughly a 76% chance of a September rate increase.
